3. The case of the pre-emptor, in short, is that 4.86 acres of land of Plot Nos.4683/4684/4686/4694/4695/4707/47 43/4748/488614751/4725 of S.A. Khatian No.1380 originally belonged to Behari Lal, Chandra Kanta Saha and Bashanta Kumar Saha to the extent of six annas two gondas two karas, eight annas and one anna seventeen gondas two karas share respectively. Chandra Kanta Saha died leaving behind 3 sons China Ranjan, Nitya Ranjan and Sukhu Ranjan Saha. Sulchu Ranjan Saha sold his share to Nitya Ranjan by kabala dated 09.03.1983 who sold two decimals land along with other lands to the pre-emptor and A. Sobhan, A. Khalque and A. Kader. Chitta Ranjan sold equal quantity of land to the pre-emptor and the aforesaid three persons, Abdul Khaleque and Abdul Kader sold their share to the pre-emptor by kabala dated 31.07.1985. Chatta Ranjan Saha and Nitya Ranjan Saha by two kabalas 07.07.1983 sold their shares to Md. Eunus Hawlader and Fazlul Huq who sold their purchased land to the pre-emptor by two kabalas dated 03.03.1987. Aforesaid Abdus Sobhan sold his interest on 13.02.1993 to the pre-emptor and Nitya Ranjan Saha sold 14 decimals land on 05.08.1993 to the pre-emptor and thus, the pre-emptor is a co-sharer by purchase of each plot of S.A. Khatian No. 1380. Most Taherunnessa and other sold 57 decimal land from the above khatian on 26.05.1984 and 27.05.1984 measuring an area of 28'/2 plus 281/2 decimals in tota1.57 decimals land to Md. Haider Parvez, opposite party No.05 who possessed the same by constructing a house thereon. Haider Parvez by a kabala dated 08.01.1995 sold his 57 decimals land along with structure to pre-emptee Nos.1- 4 who are strangers showing higher value at Tk.3,00,000/- only. But to avoid complication, the pre-emptor deposited the entire consideration money along with statutory compensation as shown in the deed with a claim for returning back Tk. 1,00,000/- if the pre-emptees failed prove that actually Tk.4,00,000/- was paid. The pre-emptor has possessed the adjacent land of each side of the case land. The pre-emptor urgently needed the case land, that the impugned sale was held beyond the knowledge of the pre-emptor. If the pre-emptor was tendered or could learn before the transfer then certainly he would have purchased the same that the pre-emptor had no good relation with the vendor. The pre-emptor came to know about the transfer on 10.01.1995 and have filed the case on 30.01.1995 by depositing the consideration money as shown in the deed along with statutory compensation. 

 4. Opposite party Nos.1-4 contested the case by filing written objection all the material allegations made in the application and contended, inter alia, that the pre-emptor has no locus standi to file the pre-emption application. The pre-emptor sustained no loss and injury by the impugned kabala, that the case land is situated in a compact block within pucca boundary wall that the pre-emptor has no land beside it. The pre-emptor has no necessity of the case land. The case is filed at the instance and ill advice of one Jalal Ahmed. The pre-emptor married twice and he has been lying in America with his first wife from a long time. The actual price of the sale was TK.9,00,000/- out of which 4 lace was for the land and the rest five lacs for the building which was written in a separate deed. The pre-emptor's case suffers from short deposit. The pre-emptor was a good friend of the vendor who recommended for transfer to the pre-emptees and he had previous knowledge about the transfer, that the scribe, identifier and attesting witnesses of the impugned deed are party men of the pre-emptor. There is a building consisting of 8 rooms in the case land, the case land was demarcated with the consent of the co-sharers and the land of plot Nos.4687/4688 are situated to the north of the case land which belonged to one Lutfunahar Begum. It is to the east of Pourasava Road and to the west there is the land of Mir Tazem Ali. The vendor opened a separate holding in the Pourasava and electricity connection was installed therein. A separate new Khatian with the consent of the co-sharers being khatian No.1380/6 was opened in Misc. Case No.90pk/1984 and order dated 26.11.1994. The vendor firstly mutated nature Case No.15PK11985-86. The pre-emptees incurred Tk. 1,05,000/- as development cost. There was a Bainapatra with the Vendor dated 14.12.1994 of that day Tk. 1,00,000/- was paid on 08.01.1995 out of which Tk.1,90,000/- by cash and Tk.5,55,000/- was paid through cheque. 

 "I. For that the High Court Division has committed an error of law in not considering that S.A Khatian No.1380 is mentioned in the schedule of the disputed deed dated 08.01.1995 and the said fact was admitted by both the parties but erroneously held that the pre- emptor appellant has lost his right of pre-emption by separation of joint holding vide separate Khatian No.1380/6 in the name of respondent No.5 which has supposed to be subsequent creation after filing of the instant miscellaneous case and therefore, the impugned order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. 

 9. Mrs. Nahid Yeasmin, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellant, submits that the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division has committed an error of law in not considering that S.A Khatian No.1380 is mentioned in the schedule of the disputed deed dated 08.01.1995 and the said fact was admitted by both the parties but erroneously held that the pre-emptor appellant has lost his right of preemption by separation of joint holding vide separate Khatian No.1380/6 in the name of respondent No.5 which has supposed to be subsequent creation after filing of the instant miscellaneous pre-emption case and therefore, the impugned order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. She further submits that the High Court Division has committed an error of law in observing that separation of the joint holding, the other co-sharers ceased to be co-sharers and they have lost their right of pre-emption without considering that admittedly no notice was served upon the co-sharer in a mutation proceedings of the disputed jama and as such, order of sub-division of the tenancy will be bad and not be binding on the non-notified co-sharer tenants and therefore, the pre-emptor did not cease to be co-sharer in the joint tenancy and as such, the impugned order is liable to be set aside. 

 12. In the instant pre-emption petition, it appears that the disputed land measuring on area 0.57 acre appertaining to S.A Khatian No.1380 has been recorded as nul land but since the same has been fallen in the Patuakhali Pouro Area, the same is to be treated as Non-Agricultural land. 

 14. The respondent-opposite party has come with a further allegation that appellant-pre-emptor was a co-sharer in SA Khatian No.1380 but before execution and registration case kabala the disputed jama has been separated through a mutation case and a new Khatian being No.1380/6 has been created and as such, their co-sharership has been ceased and as such, they have lost the right of pre-emption. On perusal of the materials on record, it appears that in the present case, the vendor of the opposite party No.5 was Tahenumessa. She along with others purchased five annas eight gonads and three karas share from the recorded tenant Behari Lal who was the owner of six annas two gondas two kara share. She along with others on 28.12.1983 mutated their jama by filing mutation Case No.605 PK of 1983-84. After separation of holding the other co-sharers ceased to be co-sharers and as such, the pre-emptors have lost their right of pre-emption. On the other hand, he along with Abdus Sabhan mutated his name on 14.08.1986 in mutation Case No.83 PK of 1986-87 and separate Khatian has been prepared in their names. All these facts have been clearly noted S.A. Khatian No. 1380 which has been marked Ext. No.4 by the trial Court. 

 15. Opposite party No.5, Md. Hyder Parvez, after purchase from Taherunnessa, mutated his name on 14.07.1985 through Mutation Case No.15 PK of 1985-86 and separate Khatian No.1380/6 was prepared in his name. It does not mean that the jama has not been separated and all the co-sharers of SA Khatian No.1380 are entitled to get notice of this mutation proceeding. The jama has already been separated through the mutation case. So, this pre-emptor petitioner has no scope to challenge the mutation proceeding of opposite party No.5, Md. Ryder Parvez. It further appears from the deed of the petitioner, it is clear that he has purchased the land from Plot No.4679 but not from the case Plot No.4686. 

 17. On the other hand, the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the respondent (opposite party) argued that the seller opposite party No.5 Md. Hyder Parvez after nurchase from Taherunnessa mutated his name on 14.07.1985 in Mutation Case No.15 PK of 1985-86 and separated Khatian No.1380/6 in his name and as such, the jama has been separated and all the co-sharers of SA Khatian No.1380 are entitled to get notice of this mutation proceeding and since the jama has alreadz been separated in the above mutation case, this pre-emptor has no scope to challenge the mutation proceeding of opposite party No.5, Md. Hyder Parvez, further from the deed of the petitioner, it is clear that he has purchased the land from Plot No.4679 but not from the case Plot No.4686 and thus, this appeal is liable to be dismissed.
